web_evidence.title: The Corrections
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained authorized opening narrates Alfred and Enid externally in third person; its initial you could feel it is atmospheric and generic.

web_evidence.title: New Sincerity and the Contemporary American Family Novel
web_evidence.note: Scholarly structural analysis explicitly identifies an uninvolved third-person narrator and explains the novel-wide variable internal focalization across the Lambert characters.

web_evidence.title: “He stopped to lower his window and say hello”: Jonathan Franzen, Neorealism and De-politicized Communitarianism
web_evidence.note: Peer-reviewed analysis describes The Corrections as using a third-person omniscient, heterodiegetic narrator across chapters focalized through different Lambert family members.

web_evidence.title: The Corrections Literary Elements
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies an anonymous third-person narrator whose focal character changes by section.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person: numerous substantial quotes sustain external he/she narration while entering the private consciousness of Chip, Enid, Alfred, Gary, and Denise. Web evidence explains this pattern as variable internal focalization or free-indirect discourse under an uninvolved third-person narrator, so changes of focal character are not person alternation. The many generic uses of you are aphoristic or free-indirect generalizations rather than a sustained second-person protagonist, and the first-person material in q00869 and q00882 is dialogue. The authorized excerpt covers only the opening, but two scholarly whole-book analyses independently establish the same structure; no material contrary evidence remains.
